definition:
v. 放弃，抛弃，遗弃


搭配：abandon a plan/hope, abandon oneself to
etymology: a-(表加强或进入) + bandon(控制，管辖) = 置于管辖之外 = 放弃、抛弃
sentence_en: The crew had to abandon the sinking ship as the fierce storm intensified.
sentence_zh: 随着猛烈的风暴加剧，船员们不得不弃船逃生。

definition:
v. 降低，使卑下，贬抑


搭配：abase oneself, abase one's pride
etymology: a-(向，使) + base(低下的，基础的) = 使变得低下 = 降低，贬抑
sentence_en: He refused to abase himself before the corrupt officials.
sentence_zh: 他拒绝在腐败官员面前卑躬屈膝。

definition:
v. 使羞愧，使局促不安


搭配：abash sb., look abashed
etymology: a-(加强语气) + bash(打击，击碎) = 精神受到打击而感到羞愧或局促不安
sentence_en: She was not at all abashed by the difficult questions asked by the professor.
sentence_zh: 她丝毫没有被教授提出的刁钻问题弄得局促不安。

definition:
v. 减轻，减弱，缓和


搭配：abate the storm, the pain abates
etymology: a-(向下，减少) + bat(打，击) = 向下打压 = 减轻、减弱
sentence_en: We waited for the storm to abate before continuing our mountain hike.
sentence_zh: 我们等暴风雨减弱后才继续进行我们的山地徒步。

definition:
v. 退位，放弃（权力、责任等）


搭配：abdicate the throne, abdicate responsibility
etymology: ab-(离开，脱离) + dic(宣布，命令) + -ate(动词后缀) = 宣告脱离职位 = 退位、放弃
sentence_en: The king was forced to abdicate the throne after the political revolution.
sentence_zh: 在政治革命之后，国王被迫宣布退位。

definition:
n. 腹部，下腹


搭配：lower abdomen, abdominal pain
etymology: abdomen(拉丁语，指人体腹部)
sentence_en: The patient experienced sharp pain in the lower abdomen.
sentence_zh: 病人感到下腹部剧烈疼痛。

definition:
v. 绑架，拐走，诱拐


搭配：abduct a child, be abducted by terrorists
etymology: ab-(离开，离去) + duct(引导，拉) = 拉开，带走 = 绑架、拐走
sentence_en: The wealthy businessman was abducted on his way home from work.
sentence_zh: 这位富商在下班回家的路上遭到绑架。

definition:
adj. 越轨的，异常的，畸变的


搭配：aberrant behavior, aberrant chromosomes
etymology: ab-(离开，偏离) + err(犯错，游荡) + -ant(形容词后缀) = 偏离正轨的 = 异常的、变态的
sentence_en: Scientists noticed aberrant patterns in the climate data that required careful analysis.
sentence_zh: 科学家们注意到气候数据中存在需要仔细分析的异常模式。

definition:
v. 教唆，唆使，协助（犯罪）


搭配：abet a crime, aid and abet
etymology: a-(表加强) + bet(古英语词根，意为刺激、煽动，源自日耳曼语族)
sentence_en: He was arrested for helping to plan and abet the bank robbery.
sentence_zh: 他因涉嫌策划和教唆银行抢劫案而被捕。

definition:
v. 痛恨，厌恶，憎恶


搭配：abhor violence, abhor cruelty
etymology: ab-(离开，远离) + horr(颤抖，恐惧，源自horrere) = 吓得倒退、极其厌恶
sentence_en: True scientists abhor dishonesty and manipulation of experimental results.
sentence_zh: 真正的科学家痛恨不诚实以及对实验结果的操纵。

definition:
v. 遵守，坚持；忍受，容忍


搭配：abide by the rules, cannot abide sb.
etymology: a-(表加强) + bide(停留，居住) = 留下来等待或承担 = 遵守、忍受
sentence_en: All members of the committee must abide by the agreed regulations.
sentence_zh: 委员会的所有成员都必须遵守商定的规章制度。

definition:
adj. 可怜的，悲惨的；卑劣的，绝望的


搭配：abject poverty, abject apology
etymology: ab-(向下) + ject(投掷，扔) = 被向下扔出去的 = 卑微的、凄惨的
sentence_en: Millions of people around the world still live in conditions of abject poverty.
sentence_zh: 世界上仍有数百万人生活在极端贫困的境地中。

definition:
v. 发誓放弃，公开放弃（信仰、权利等）


搭配：abjure a belief, abjure allegiance
etymology: ab-(离开) + jur(发誓，法律) = 发誓断绝关系 = 公开放弃
sentence_en: To gain citizenship, the applicant had to formally abjure loyalty to his former country.
sentence_zh: 为了获得公民身份，申请人必须正式宣誓放弃对原先国家的效忠。

definition:
adj. / n. （语法）夺格的，表剥离或方所的格


搭配：ablative case, ablative absolute
etymology: ab-(分离，取走) + lat(带走，携带) + -ive(形容词后缀) = 带有移走、分离含义的语法格
sentence_en: In Latin grammar, the ablative case is used to indicate separation or source.
sentence_zh: 在拉丁语语法中，夺格用来表示分离或来源。

definition:
adj. 着火的，燃烧的；闪耀的，激昂的


搭配：set ablaze, ablaze with lights
etymology: a-(处于...状态) + blaze(火焰，闪光) = 处于烈火或闪耀状态中
sentence_en: The historic downtown building was set ablaze by the massive explosion.
sentence_zh: 这座历史悠久 市中心建筑被巨大的爆炸化为一片火海。

definition:
adj. 体魄强健的，健康的，健全的


搭配：able-bodied workers, able-bodied adults
etymology: able(有能力的) + bodied(有身体的) = 身体强健、有劳动能力的
sentence_en: The project requires dozens of able-bodied workers to lift heavy construction materials.
sentence_zh: 该项目需要几十名身强力壮的工人来搬运沉重的建筑材料。

definition:
n. 洗澡，净手，洗礼仪式


搭配：perform ablutions, morning ablutions
etymology: ab-(洗去，离开) + lut(冲洗，洗涤，源自luere) + -ion(名词后缀) = 洗净污秽
sentence_en: The monks gathered by the river to perform their daily ritual ablutions.
sentence_zh: 僧侣们聚集在河边进行每日的常规净手和沐浴仪式。

definition:
v. 放弃，克制，拒绝（权利、欲望等）


搭配：abnegate pleasure, abnegate self-interest
etymology: ab-(否定，离开) + neg(否定，拒绝，源自negare) + -ate(动词后缀) = 彻底拒绝或放弃
sentence_en: Monks often abnegate worldly pleasures in search of spiritual enlightenment.
sentence_zh: 僧侣们为了寻求精神觉悟，常常克制世俗的欢愉。

definition:
adj. 反常的，不规则的，异常的


搭配：abnormal behavior, abnormal weather conditions
etymology: ab-(偏离，远离) + normal(正常的) = 偏离正常标准的 = 异常的
sentence_en: Meteorologists recorded abnormal rainfall amounts across the region this summer.
sentence_zh: 气象学家记录到今年夏天该地区的降雨量异常。

definition:
n. 住所，住宅，寓所


搭配：permanent abode, humble abode
etymology: a-(表状态) + bode(bide的过去式，居住、逗留) = 居住的地方
sentence_en: After years of traveling, the artist finally settled down in a cozy woodland abode.
sentence_zh: 经过多年的游历，这位艺术家最终定居在林间一处舒适的住宅里。

definition:
v. 废除，废止（法律、制度、习俗等）


搭配：abolish slavery, abolish a law
etymology: ab-(离开) + ol(生长，源自olescere) + -ish(动词后缀) = 使不再生长，使其消亡 = 废除
sentence_en: The international community pushed for governments to abolish outdated trade tariffs.
sentence_zh: 国际社会敦促各国政府废除过时的贸易关税。

definition:
n. 废除，废止


搭配：the abolition of slavery, abolition movement
etymology: abolish(废除) + -ion(名词后缀) = 废除，废止
sentence_en: The 19th century witnessed a powerful movement dedicated to the abolition of slavery.
sentence_zh: 19世纪见证了一场致力于废除奴隶制的强大运动。

definition:
adj. 可恶的，讨厌的，极坏的


搭配：abominable weather, abominable crime
etymology: ab-(加强) + omin(凶兆，不祥，源自omen) + -able(可……的) = 像凶兆般让人厌恶的 = 可恶的
sentence_en: The prisoners were subjected to abominable conditions during their captivity.
sentence_zh: 囚犯在被关押期间遭受了极其恶劣的待遇。

definition:
v. 痛恨，厌恶


搭配：abominate cruelty, abominate lying
etymology: ab- + omin(不祥之兆) + -ate(动词后缀) = 视同不祥而极度痛恨
sentence_en: She confessed that she did abominate any form of deceit in scientific research.
sentence_zh: 她坦言自己极其痛恨科学研究中的任何欺骗行为。

definition:
adj. / n. 土著的，原住民的


搭配：aboriginal tribes, aboriginal culture
etymology: ab-(从……起) + origine(起源，源头) + -al(形容词后缀) = 自古以来就在该源头生存的 = 土著的
sentence_en: The museum displays artifacts that reflect the long history of aboriginal Australians.
sentence_zh: 博物馆陈列着反映澳大利亚土著悠久历史的文物。

definition:
v. 夭折，中途失败；流产，堕胎


搭配：abort a mission, abort a pregnancy
etymology: ab-(离去，偏离) + ort(出生，源自oriri) = 未能正常出生 = 中途流产或中止
sentence_en: The pilot had to abort the takeoff due to a sudden engine warning.
sentence_zh: 由于突然的发动机警报，飞行员不得不中止起飞。

definition:
n. 人工流产，堕胎；（计划等的）夭折


搭配：have an abortion, debate on abortion
etymology: abort(流产) + -ion(名词后缀) = 流产，堕胎
sentence_en: The legal and ethical debate surrounding abortion remains deeply divisive worldwide.
sentence_zh: 围绕堕胎的法律和伦理争论在全球范围内依然存在巨大分歧。

definition:
adj. 徒劳的，失败的，夭折的


搭配：abortive attempt, abortive negotiations
etymology: abort(流产，夭折) + -ive(形容词后缀) = 像流产一样未见成效的 = 徒劳的
sentence_en: After several abortive attempts to cross the river, the expedition team changed route.
sentence_zh: 在数次试图渡河无果后，考察队改变了路线。

definition:
v. 富于，充满；大量存在


搭配：opportunities abound, abound in/with
etymology: a-(表状态) + bound(波浪，源自undare，满溢如波涛) = 泛滥、充满
sentence_en: Wildlife and rare plants abound in the remote national park.
sentence_zh: 在这个偏远的国家公园里，野生动物和珍稀植物资源极其丰富。

definition:
n. / v. （立场、政策等的）彻底改变，向后转


搭配：make an about-face, sudden about-face
etymology: about(关于，转圈) + face(脸，正面) = 脸朝向相反方向转 = 彻底转变
sentence_en: The company made a sudden about-face regarding its remote work policy.
sentence_zh: 该公司对远程办公政策来了一个180度的大转弯。

definition:
adj. / adv. 光明正大的，坦诚的，无欺诈的


搭配：keep things aboveboard, completely aboveboard
etymology: above(在……上方) + board(牌桌，甲板) = 手牌放在桌面上让人看见，不搞阴谋诡计 = 光明正大的
sentence_en: The auditor confirmed that all financial transactions of the startup were entirely aboveboard.
sentence_zh: 审计师确认该初创公司的所有金融交易都完全公开透明、合法合规。

definition:
n. 磨损，擦伤，表面磨损


搭配：skin abrasion, resistance to abrasion
etymology: ab-(离开，磨掉) + ras(刮，擦，源自radere) + -ion(名词后缀) = 刮擦磨损
sentence_en: The cyclist suffered minor abrasions after falling off his bike on the gravel road.
sentence_zh: 骑行者在砂石路上摔下自行车后，身体有多处轻微擦伤。

definition:
adj. 粗鲁的，伤感情的；研磨的，摩擦的


搭配：abrasive personality, abrasive cleaner
etymology: abras(擦伤，磨损) + -ive(形容词后缀) = 具有磨损性的，性格刻薄刺人的
sentence_en: Despite his abrasive manner, he was recognized as a brilliant scientist.
sentence_zh: 尽管他为人态度生硬、言语刻薄，但人们公认他是一位杰出的科学家。

definition:
adv. 并肩地，并排地；紧跟（时代、潮流）


搭配：keep abreast of, walk abreast
etymology: a-(处于) + breast(胸部，胸膛) = 胸膛贴着胸膛并排 = 并肩地
sentence_en: Read professional journals regularly to keep abreast of the latest technological breakthroughs.
sentence_zh: 定期阅读专业期刊，以紧跟最新的技术突破。

definition:
v. 删节，节略，缩短（书籍、文章等）


搭配：abridge a book, abridge freedom
etymology: a-(表加强) + bridge(源自breviare，变短，与short同源) = 使缩短、精简
sentence_en: The publisher decided to abridge the massive novel so younger readers could enjoy it.
sentence_zh: 出版商决定对这部宏大的长篇小说进行删节，以便年轻读者能够阅读。

definition:
v. 正式废除，撤销（法律、协议、习惯）


搭配：abrogate a treaty, abrogate a law
etymology: ab-(离开) + rog(要求，提议，源自rogare) + -ate(动词后缀) = 取消原先提出的法令 = 废除
sentence_en: The two nations met to abrogate the outdated trade treaty signed decades ago.
sentence_zh: 两国会晤以废除几十年前签署的过时贸易条约。

definition:
adj. 突然的，意外的；唐突的，生硬的


搭配：abrupt change, abrupt ending
etymology: ab-(离开，剥离) + rupt(断裂，破裂) = 突然断开的 = 突然的、生硬的
sentence_en: The lecture came to an abrupt stop when the campus power grid failed.
sentence_zh: 当校园电网故障时，讲座戛然而止。

definition:
n. 脓肿，疮疡


搭配：dental abscess, form an abscess
etymology: ab-(离开，分离) + scedere/cess(离去，积聚) = 体内组织溃烂积脓的地方
sentence_en: The dentist had to treat the painful tooth abscess before performing root canal surgery.
sentence_zh: 牙医在做根管治疗之前，必须先治疗疼痛的牙脓肿。

definition:
n. （数学）横坐标


搭配：x-axis abscissa, coordinate grid
etymology: ab-(离开) + sciss(切割，剪开，源自scindere) + -a(名词后缀) = 被坐标轴切割出的水平截段 = 横坐标
sentence_en: On the scatter plot, the horizontal axis represents the abscissa while the vertical axis represents the ordinate.
sentence_zh: 在散点图上，水平轴代表横坐标，垂直轴代表纵坐标。

definition:
v. 潜逃，逃跑，畏罪潜逃


搭配：abscond with money, abscond from custody
etymology: ab-(离开) + scond(藏匿，隐藏，源自condere) = 藏起来并悄悄溜走 = 潜逃
sentence_en: The dishonest accountant managed to abscond with millions of dollars of company funds.
sentence_zh: 那个不诚实的会计设法携款数百万美元公司资金潜逃。

definition:
n. 缺席，不在；缺乏，缺少


搭配：in the absence of, leave of absence
etymology: ab-(离开) + sent(存在，源自esse) + -ence(名词后缀) = 离去了、不存在 = 缺席、缺乏
sentence_en: In the absence of concrete evidence, the jury could not convict the suspect.
sentence_zh: 在缺乏确凿证据的情况下，陪审团无法给嫌疑人定罪。

definition:
adj. 缺席的，不在的；心不在焉的


搭配：absent from class, absent-minded
etymology: ab-(离开) + sent(存在的) = 不在现场的 = 缺席的
sentence_en: Several students were absent from the lecture due to a sudden flu outbreak.
sentence_zh: 由于突然爆发流感，有几名学生缺席了讲座。

definition:
adj. 绝对的，完全的；无限制的


搭配：absolute truth, absolute power
etymology: ab-(完全) + solv/solut(解开，松开) = 从约束中完全解脱出来的 = 绝对的、无限制的
sentence_en: The research findings offer absolute proof that the hypothesis was correct.
sentence_zh: 研究结果提供了绝对的证据，证明该假设是正确的。

definition:
n. 免罪，赦免，宽恕


搭配：seek absolution, grant absolution
etymology: absolute(解除约束) + -ion(名词后缀) = 解除惩罚与罪责 = 赦免
sentence_en: He went to the old priest hoping to find spiritual absolution for his past mistakes.
sentence_zh: 他去找那位老神父，希望能为自己过去的错误找到精神上的宽恕。

definition:
v. 免除，宣告无罪，赦免


搭配：absolve sb. from blame, absolve of guilt
etymology: ab-(离开，脱离) + solve(解开，松开) = 解开罪责并使其离开 = 宣告无罪、免除责任
sentence_en: The independent inquiry report served to absolve the director of any direct wrongdoing.
sentence_zh: 独立调查报告起到了为该主任洗脱直接不当行为责任的作用。

definition:
v. 吸收（液体、光、热等）；吸引全部注意力，理解


搭配：absorb knowledge, absorb shock
etymology: ab-(向内，向下) + sorb(吞咽，喝，源自sorbere) = 吞入、吸纳
sentence_en: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere during the process of photosynthesis.
sentence_zh: 植物在光合作用过程中吸收大气中的二氧化碳。

definition:
adj. / n. 能吸收的；吸水材料


搭配：absorbent material, absorbent cotton
etymology: absorb(吸收) + -ent(形容词后缀，表具备特性的) = 具吸收能力的
sentence_en: The laboratory technician used highly absorbent paper towels to clean up the spilled chemical.
sentence_zh: 实验室技术员用吸水性极强的纸巾清理了泼洒的化学试剂。

definition:
n. 吸收；专心，全神贯注


搭配：absorption of nutrients, total absorption
etymology: absorb的变形名词形式 = 吸收过程或全神贯注的状态
sentence_en: The efficient absorption of vitamins depends heavily on a balanced daily diet.
sentence_zh: 维生素的高效吸收很大程度上取决于均衡的日常饮食。

definition:
v. 戒除，禁绝；（投票时）弃权


搭配：abstain from voting, abstain from alcohol
etymology: ab-(离开) + tain(握住，持有，源自tenere) = 保持距离不去触碰 = 戒除、弃权
sentence_en: Several member states chose to abstain from voting on the controversial resolution.
sentence_zh: 几个成员国选择对这项有争议的决议投弃权票。

definition:
adj. 有节制的，饮食有度的，简朴的


搭配：abstemious lifestyle, abstemious diet
etymology: ab-(离开) + temetum(含酒精的饮料) + -ous(形容词后缀) = 远离烈酒、克制饮食的 = 有节制的
sentence_en: Despite attending lavish banquets, the philosopher maintained an exceptionally abstemious diet.
sentence_zh: 尽管出席了盛大的宴会，这位哲学家依然保持着极其有节制的饮食习惯。

definition:
n. 节制，禁欲，戒绝


搭配：total abstinence, practice abstinence
etymology: abstain(戒除)的名词形式 = 克制、戒绝
sentence_en: Medical professionals often recommend complete abstinence from smoking to lower health risks.
sentence_zh: 医学专家通常建议彻底戒烟以降低健康风险。
